headline: Sunny, dry and milder-than-normal weather lasts through Saturday, then a coastal storm is looking more likely to bring wind and soaking rain to New York City and the surrounding area late Sunday into Monday, with the wettest computer models showing enough rain for flooding.

sections.title: Today & Tonight
sections.text: Thursday afternoon stays mostly sunny and dry in New York City under strong high pressure, with light winds under about 10 mph turning southwest (possibly more southerly with a sea breeze) and a few thin high clouds drifting in late. A weak disturbance passes overhead tonight into Friday morning without rain, and clear skies with light winds let outlying areas get quite cold while the city stays milder. Patchy freezing fog is possible tonight in river valleys, sheltered inland spots and the Long Island Pine Barrens, bringing a low chance of black ice on bridges and overpasses.

sections.title: Short Term
sections.text: Friday stays sunny and dry, and the dry air lets temperatures climb quickly into the 60s. On Saturday, winds turn to blow in off the ocean as the high pressure moves offshore, so highs are lower than Friday but still several degrees above normal. As the air slowly gets more humid over the next few days, overnight fog becomes more likely in outlying areas, especially river valleys.

sections.title: Long Term
sections.text: Forecasters are growing more confident that at least some rain falls sometime Sunday into Monday as a coastal storm moves in late Sunday, with rain and lower clouds possible Sunday, rain likely early Monday, and improvement possible Monday afternoon with northwest gusts around 25–30 mph. The storm could have some tropical or subtropical traits, so the National Hurricane Center is worth checking; the American and Canadian models favor a wet, single-storm scenario, with one AI-based model showing a swath of about 4 inches of rain from the Mid-Atlantic to southern New England, while the European model remains an outlier. Since about 3 inches in 6 hours is enough to cause flooding here, the wetter scenario could mean widespread minor flooding and isolated flash flooding in the most flood-prone spots. Peak wind gusts are estimated at 30–40 mph, but could be higher if the storm deepens and tracks close to the coast.

coast: Winds and seas stay below Small Craft Advisory levels through Saturday with high pressure nearby. Winds and waves build Sunday into Monday as the coastal storm approaches, with ocean seas reaching 5 ft or more by late Sunday and gale-force winds possible on all waters Monday, depending on the storm's track and strength. Higher-than-usual tides around Tuesday's full moon could bring minor coastal flooding depending on the storm's track and intensity, and one coastal flood model ensemble already hints at minor flooding Sunday night.
watch_for: The track and timing of the late Sunday–Monday coastal storm, which will decide how much rain, wind and coastal flooding New York City gets.
Heavy rain of around 4 inches in the wettest scenarios, which could cause widespread minor flooding and isolated flash flooding.
Patchy freezing fog and a low chance of black ice on bridges and overpasses in valleys and sheltered inland areas tonight.
confidence: Forecasters are confident in dry, mild weather through Saturday and increasingly confident in some rain Sunday into Monday, but the storm's track, timing, rain totals and winds remain uncertain.
